messages.subject: stan model scalability
parts:

Can anybody share an experience of stan model scalability, i.e. how computational time increases with increasing data set size.  It is interesting to see if such experiments were done for simple stan models and stan pk/pd models which involve the solution of differential equations. 

Thanks,

Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan model scalability
parts:
Scalability really varies with the size of data and complexity
of the model, which can be related. Scaling can even be sublinear
in cases where the model is well specified and the data are i.i.d.,
because much of the work that's done per parameter is fixed and
the additional data help constrain the posterior to something nicely
shaped for sampling (roughly normal).

That axis should be seconds/draw, not seconds/sample! And it's
for a pretty simple problem.

Andrew's still training me to say that a sample is a sequence
of draws. And that a sample has a size.

- Bob
